sections.h2: Where is Brown County, Ohio, and where do deeds get recorded?
sections.html:
Brown County lies along Ohio's southern boundary, where the Ohio River divides it from Kentucky. Georgetown is the county seat. The recorder works out of the Administration Building, 800 Mt. Orab Pike, Suite 151, Georgetown, Ohio 45121. The auditor (Suite 181) and treasurer (Suite 171) are in the same building.

Wikipedia gives 493 square miles and a creation date of March 1, 1818, cut from Adams and Clermont counties. Early settlers included the father of Ulysses S. Grant, who ran a tannery near Georgetown. Burley tobacco was first grown near Higginsport. Villages include Aberdeen, Fayetteville, Hamersville, Higginsport, Mount Orab, Ripley, Russellville and Sardinia, and Lake Waynoka and Lake Lorelei are census-designated places.

The Census Bureau counted 43,676 residents in 2020 and estimates 44,397 for July 2025. The Census QuickFacts table lists 19,965 housing units, with 77.2 percent lived in by owners and a median owned-home value of $196,200. The Census lists a 33.9-minute mean trip to work, and Wikipedia places the county in the Cincinnati metropolitan statistical area.

sections.h2: How much does the Brown County Recorder charge?
sections.html:
Per the recorder's fee page, the State of Ohio sets recording charges: half is the basic fee and half goes to the Ohio Housing Trust Fund (sections 317.32 and 317.36). Most common documents share one price.

Brown County Recorder fees for common documents
ItemFee
Deed, mortgage, lease or affidavit, up to two pages$39.00
Each additional page or attachment$8.00
Non-standard document$20.00 per document
Plat, 18 by 24 inches$50.40
Copy, per page$2.00
Certified copy, per page$2.00, plus $1.00 for the seal
UCC financing statement$12.00 plus $4.00 per name indexed

Source: Brown County Recorder fee page.

Federal tax liens cost $5.00 and releases $3.00. A living will or health care power of attorney is $40.00 to record, and one certified copy of a veteran's discharge is free. The page also links the Medicaid estate recovery notice of pending transfer of property.

sections.h2: What belongs on a Brown County deed before it is recorded?
sections.html:
The recorder's how-to page lists nine items that should be on a deed before it arrives:

  • The Tax Map office stamp approving the transfer.
  • The auditor's transfer endorsement.
  • The name of the seller.
  • The name and address of the buyer.
  • The seller's original signature and the date, with the name typed or printed beneath.
  • A notary acknowledgement.
  • A legal description naming the county, the township or village and the size of the land.
  • The parcel number.
  • A preparation statement.

The staff neither prepare documents nor sell forms, and legal advice is off the table. Most sellers have a title company or attorney draft it.

The fee page adds that a conveyance or exemption form is required with transfers and that parcel identification numbers are required on every deed. The non-standard fee applies unless a document has 10-point or larger type, letter or legal paper, black or blue ink and no highlighting, with 1-inch side and bottom margins and 3 inches at the top of the first page.

sections.h2: Which documents does the Brown County Recorder accept?
sections.html:
The recorder's document types page groups what the office handles. For a seller the relevant groups are:

  • Deeds: warranty, survivorship, quit claim and sheriff's deeds, and certificates of transfer.
  • Mortgages, with releases, assignments, assumptions, subordinations and amendments.
  • Land contracts, affidavits, easements and leases.
  • Plats and condominium drawings.
  • Powers of attorney, trusts and bills of sale.
  • Liens, including mechanic's liens, federal tax liens and homeowner association liens, along with notices of commencement.

The office also files military service discharges, zoning resolutions with maps, annexations and street name changes. Anything that touches a house sale and sits in the public record, from an old mortgage to a lien, was filed through this counter.

sections.h2: What is the order of offices for a Brown County deed?
sections.html:
The recorder's page sets out two routes, and on both the deed passes through the auditor and the county's Tax Map department.

  • In person. Start at the recorder's office, which checks the document for its own requirements and fees. Next go to the auditor's office next door to complete the conveyance. The Tax Map department then picks up the deed at the Engineer Building, 25 Veterans Blvd., Georgetown.
  • By mail. Send the deed to the recorder at the Suite 151 address with a cover note and a phone number, a check payable to Brown County Recorder, all auditor fees and forms, and a self-addressed stamped envelope.

Tax Map reviews documents in the order received, so the office says a deed cannot be walked through. Legal descriptions are checked there, and the recorder advises calling the department for its requirements. Once Tax Map and the auditor have stamped the deed, it returns to the recorder to be recorded. The auditor can answer questions at 937-378-6398.

sections.h2: What are the transfer fee and conveyance tax in Brown County?
sections.html:
Look to the recorder's fee page for the local number: $4.00 of transfer fee and conveyance tax on each $1,000 of purchase price, plus fifty cents per parcel number for the auditor. A conveyance or exemption form goes with every transfer.

Two statutes sit behind that figure. The auditor's statement-of-value fee is set in section 319.54(G)(3). Separately, section 322.02 allows a county to levy a deed transfer tax of no more than 30 cents per $100. The seller named in the deed owes that tax, and it is paid to the auditor before recording. Exempt transfers, such as family gifts, file an exemption statement rather than a value statement.

Ask the auditor which exemption box fits before you sign the deed.

sections.h2: How do taxes affect a Brown County sale?
sections.html:
Property tax is paid to the county treasurer (937-378-6705), whose weekday hours run 8:00 to 4:00. Brown County's 2025 real estate bills were payable February 11, 2026 and July 31, 2026. The later second-half date followed Ohio House Bill 186, which set up an inflation cap credit on certain school district levies and applied it back to tax year 2025.

The treasurer also handles payment plans for owners who fall behind, and runs a monthly escrow program that lets owners spread payments ahead of the bill. Online payment carries convenience fees, including $1.50 for an electronic check. The auditor's site lists 35,315 parcels in the county and notes that the homestead exemption, not any federal program, is the relief available to seniors, disabled owners and qualifying disabled veterans.

Have the title company get the parcel's balance from the treasurer before the closing date.

faqs.q: What is the Brown County recording fee for a deed?
faqs.a: A deed of two pages or fewer is $39.00 on the fee page, and each added page or attachment is $8.00. Non-standard paper adds $20.00. The amounts come from section 317.32.

faqs.q: What is the mailing address for a Brown County deed?
faqs.a: Mail it to the Brown County Recorder, 800 Mt. Orab Pike, Suite 151, Georgetown, OH 45121. Include a cover note with your phone number, a check payable to Brown County Recorder, the auditor's fees and forms, and a stamped return envelope.

faqs.q: What is the conveyance tax in Brown County?
faqs.a: The page shows $4.00 per $1,000 of price, with the auditor's fifty-cent charge on each parcel number. Call the auditor at 937-378-6398 with questions, since the conveyance or exemption form must go with every transfer.

faqs.q: Does the Brown County Recorder prepare deeds?
faqs.a: No. Staff do not draft documents or sell forms, and they cannot advise on legal questions. A lawyer or title company drafts the deed. It then clears Tax Map and the auditor and only afterward reaches the recorder.

faqs.q: What were the 2026 Brown County tax due dates?
faqs.a: Real estate tax for 2025 was due February 11, 2026 (first half) and July 31, 2026 (second half, delayed because of House Bill 186). The treasurer's line, 937-378-6705, has the schedule for later years.
